page.layout: Running head at top centre; two italic epigram lines at top full width; a heading block below a rule; then one main text column of verse-like lines with a drop initial; a marginal catchword-like word at bottom right beside the last line; a small marginal mark at bottom right.

p.i: Qui simul vigilésque, somniésque: Quam doctus vigilare somniando, Tam doctus vigilando somniare.

main_text.head: DE P. MELISSI SCHEDII, Franci, insignibus, tribus videlicet liliis, partim aureis, partim argenteis, expressis.
main_text.p: TIbi lilia convenire Franco, Franca lilia consecrata genti, Non est qui merito neget, Melisse. Sed quum lilia candor ille purus Grata praecipuae ac venusta reddat, Qui fit virgineum, rogo, ut nitorem Intacta nivis aemulum nitorem, Ut lloe diuitiis ut libet metalli Sic tandem violaceis colore? An quod (maxima facultate pridem Sicut pars hominum fere assueuit) Sit candore animi tibi innocentis Argentum pretiosius vel aurum? Nequaquam, puto: quum meo Melisse Nil sit candidius, purius ve: Immo quod tibi candor ille purus, Candor ille animi sit innocentis, Quod argentum aliis, quod est et aurum, Quos inanis opum cupido ludit. Ergo vive diu, et vale, Melisse,Dum-

page.notes: Drop initial "T" in the first line is a large woodcut-style initial; the word "Ut lloe" and "Sic tandem" line are doubtful. Marginal "Dum-" at lower right is a catchword. Small mark at bottom right is a printer's or stain mark, not text. The first two lines of the verse are italic; "vigilésque" and "somniésque" as printed.
